meta.title: MeshBridge — Private device mesh and large-file transfer
meta.description: MeshBridge joins your devices into a private WireGuard mesh and moves large files directly between them — resumable, verified, never through a third party.

hero.title: Your devices, one private network.
hero.lede: MeshBridge joins the machines scattered across your home, office and cloud into a **WireGuard-encrypted private mesh**, then moves large files point-to-point between them. Speed is set by the line itself, not by someone else's relay.
hero.fine: Email verification · Self-hosted control plane · Files never touch a third party

what.title: One small server runs your network and your transfers.
what.body: Your NAS needs to send 200 GB of footage to a workstation overseas; your office server needs to sync a dataset to the cloud. Cloud drives are slow, throttled and opaque. MeshBridge runs a lightweight control plane on your own VPS, joins your devices into a private network, and keeps every transfer between the devices themselves.
what.c1Body: A self-hosted control plane built on Headscale and Tailscale. Install the agent and a device joins on its own; its 100.x address is visible only inside your network. Admission, keys and topology stay in your hands.
what.c2Body: Files move in 64 MiB chunks, each checked with BLAKE3 and tracked in a resume bitmap. Drop the connection halfway and the transfer picks up where it stopped. It only counts as done when the whole-file hash matches.
what.c3Body: Paths between devices are probed continuously. Direct whenever possible; when the network gets in the way, traffic falls back to your own relays or to object storage. A downgrade takes several consecutive samples, so a brief blip never triggers one.

principle.title: Why your files never take a detour
principle.body: MeshBridge's first rule: the control plane only coordinates (signaling, keys and scheduling), so its traffic stays in kilobytes. Files always travel on paths between your devices, and a large file that tries to squeeze through the DERP fallback is refused by the scheduler.

how.title: From sign-up to first transfer in ten minutes
how.body: No agents to configure by hand, no inbound ports to open. Everything happens in the browser, plus one command per device.
how.s1Body: Sign up with an email code, entirely in the browser. On first deployment a short wizard sets up the administrator and the mail service.
how.s2Body: The console generates one install command. Paste it on a NAS, server or workstation: Tailscale joins the network and the MeshBridge agent starts reporting in.
how.s3Body: Pick a source, a destination and a path. The scheduler chooses the best route, resumes after interruptions, and every step lands in the audit log.

closing.title: Turn the devices you own into a network of your own.
closing.body: Free to sign up · Email verification · One command per device
